en: Mount Mayon in Albay has a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape formed by repeated volcanic eruptions.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, the national bird, lives only in the forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines and a major source of hydroelectric power.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
The amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool and dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
The Philippines is a top global producer of abaca, a strong plant fiber extracted from a native banana species.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Rafflesia schadenbergiana, a parasitic plant with one of the world's largest flowers, grows in the forests of Mount Kitanglad.
The Philippine Sea contains the Philippine Trench, which plunges to a depth of over 10,500 meters below sea level.
